description.narrative: The Project Development Objective of the eTransform Project is to improve the efficiency and coverage of government service delivery using ICT.

The development objective of the e-Transform Project for Ghana is to improve the efficiency and coverage of government service delivery using information and communication technologies (ICT). The project has four components. The first component is enabling environment for electronic government and business. This component will support policies, laws, regulations, and institutional capacity building to stimulate supply and demand of electronic services with the help of a transparent, secure, and open environment, and will include revisions to the existing laws and regulations as may be necessary. It has following three sub-components: (i) storage, protection, and, opening up of government data; (ii) support for innovation centers for entrepreneurship and job creation; and (iii) institutional capacity building for policy and regulatory institutions. The second component is support for upgrading national identification system and online verification services. This component will provide support to develop a robust national identification system based on international standards to help prepare Ghana for a modern e-commerce industry, improved e-government services, and alleviate poverty. It has following two sub-components: (a) support for a national electronic identification (e-ID) system; and (b) support for digitization and integration of digital identity and verification systems into user agency operations. The third component is scale up of applications to improve service delivery in priority sectors. This component will be used to support use of ICT to improve quality and reach of services in the health and education sectors where the Government of Ghana is lagging in achieving millennium development goal (MDG), as well as to complete key e-applications currently being implemented under e-Ghana project. It has following four sub-components: (i) support for integrated e-health system in Ghana; (ii) teachers' network, educational portal, and capacity building; (iii) support for e-services; and (iv) support for existing e-applications. The fourth component is project management support. This component will support the implementation team for the overall project coordination and management, and will provide communication, procurement, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation (M and E).

condition.narrative: The Recipient shall, not later 3 months from the Effectiveness Date establish and thereafter maintain throughout the implementationof the Project, a Project Steering Committee (PSC) with a composition, mandate, terms of reference and resources satisfactory tothe Association. Without limitation to the foregoing, the PSC shall meet four times per year and shall be co-chaired by the ChiefMinisters of the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Communications, or their designees, and shall include the Chief Directorsof key participating Ministries and selected private sector representatives. The PSC will be supported by the projectimplementation unit of the Ministry of Communications on operational matters and by a Technical Committee.

title.narrative: Number of schools and health centers connected to the internet under the project
Number of teachers and students using education portals, including in rural areas, under the project

comment.narrative:
The end target value 150,000 has been be proportionately adjusted to  40,000 due to smaller scale implementation (73 SHSs in Northern regions). Achievement of the canceled of Lot 2 and Lot 3 (a total of 242 SHSs) out of the total of 315 SHSs will be supported by the Ghana Digital Acceleration Project.
This indicator has been lagged behind due to the delay from the activity r-scoping.  The Ministry of Education (MoE) requested to change the scope after WB’s No Objection to Educational portal bidding document had been issued. The rescoped assignment focuses on the Ghana Knowledge Skills Bank platform development.

It was programmed to have one public certification authority operating in Ghana under the project. The target has been achieved with the establishment of the Root CA which culminated in key ceremony performance of July 2019.

comment.narrative: The targeted three (3) tech-hubs under the project have been established and are operational.

comment.narrative: The end target value has been reduced from “90,000” to “70,000” due to the cancellation of the eJustice phase 2 (scale-up). The impact of the eJustice phase 2 will be materialized under the Ghana Digital Acceleration Project.

comment.narrative: The end target value has been reduced from “5 days” to “7 days”. The Project made significant improvement (more than 50% reduction) to issue a birth certificate from 15 days (baseline) to 7 days, however no further rigorous improvement or training support is anticipated due to reduction of capacity building/operational cost support.

title.narrative: Average days required to process a company registration

comment.narrative:
Company registration now takes 2 days while sole proprietorship registration already takes 1 day.
The end target value has been reduced from “1 day” to “2 days”. The Project made significant improvement (50% reduction) to process a company registration from 4 days (baseline) to 2 days, however no further rigorous improvement or training support isnticipated due to reduction of capacity building/operational cost support.

Number of teachers completing training through computer/internet aided education, under the project

comment.narrative: 1485 teachers (including 312 females) have been trained in ten regions, exceeding the target for the programme by 112%.

title.narrative: Number of people trained, under the project

comment.narrative: It was programmed to train 3000 persons by project end. As of now, target has been significantly exceeded with 34631  persons trained of which 17189 males and 17442 females.

title.narrative: Number of new e-Government applications providing service to the public under the project

comment.narrative: Target achieved. 7 e-Gov applications are now effectively in operation, providing services to the public. The four applications include: eJustice, eProcurement, eImmigration, and integrated system for data protection.

title.narrative: Number of locations of Government Ministries, Departments, and Agencies (MDAs) benefiting from enhanced bandwidth, under the project

comment.narrative:
So far 477 Government Institutions are benefitting from bandwidth provided under the project. This consists of 144 government institutions connected through fibre and 333 government institutions connected through LTE.
This represents 198.7% of the target set for the project.

title.narrative: Number of jobs created or sustained through the tech hubs supported by the project, including by start-ups benefiting from innovation and training grants and through online work (Number)

comment.narrative: Job creation reach beyond the end target of 100.   So far 3622 direct jobs (1635 males and 1987 females (54.8%) have been created at the Ghana Tech Lab and the Ghana Innovation Hub.
